October 20, 2026

US strikes Iran again as Trump extends Strait of Hormuz deadline

tags: war, politics, markets
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

The United States bombed Iran's Conorock naval base, the first American strike on Iran in seven weeks, wounding two Iranian soldiers according to Al Jazeera. Iran said it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the Strait of Hormuz and threatened to cut undersea global internet cables if bombing continues. President Trump then said special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had met a "respected" Iranian leader and paused planned strikes on Iranian power plants for five more days, a claim Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf denied, saying no negotiations had taken place. Oil moved sharply on the news, with Brent crude falling 10.5 percent to $100.37 a barrel after approaching $120 last week; the war, launched on Feb. 28, has killed more than 2,000 people including at least 13 US service members.

Russian drone kills infant and five others in Kharkiv region park

tags: war, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

A Russian drone struck a crowded park in Nova Vodolaha in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, killing a 14-month-old girl in a stroller along with three women and an 11-year-old girl, according to Ukrainian officials. Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said at least 15 others were wounded, including seven children. The strike came as President Trump said at the White House that "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine," blaming President Volodymyr Zelensky for obstructing a peace deal. UN monitors reported civilian casualties in Ukraine rose 85% in September year-on-year, with at least 328 killed and 2,105 injured.

Widower presses Vance on military failures in Kuwait drone strike

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @groundnews

At a CBS News town hall, Joey Amor, whose wife Army Reserve Master Sgt. Nicole Amor was killed with five other soldiers in an Iranian drone strike on the Port of Shuaiba in Kuwait on March 1, asked Vice President JD Vance whether military leaders would be held accountable. CBS News has reported that the site lacked sufficient fortifications and drone defenses, that the Army decided against moving troops farther from Iran, and that a request for additional medical support went unaddressed. Vance said it was the first he had heard of the alleged failures and pledged to investigate, adding that the military has since changed its anti-drone tactics and repositioned troops, calling the earlier placement "a huge mistake." The strike remains the deadliest attack on US forces of the war.

Hegseth held secret meeting with Netanyahu days before Israeli elections

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth met privately with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, a meeting Hegseth subsequently described as a "historic mission." The meeting took place less than a week before Israeli elections and after the United States moved additional military assets into the region and resumed strikes on Iran. Oil prices have risen sharply over the same period.

Lavrov meets Iranian foreign minister in Tehran as Moscow seeks mediator role

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi in Tehran for talks on the region's escalating crises. At a joint news conference, Araqchi said regional issues should be resolved through diplomacy and blamed the United States for insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz, calling for a joint regional security arrangement "without the presence of foreign forces." Iran's conditions for reopening the strait remain unchanged, with Araqchi saying Washington could meet them within days by complying with a ceasefire proposal presented in September.

Trump DHS appointees asked CISA to obtain and hack a voting machine

tags: politics, surveillance, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

ProPublica reported that political appointees at the Department of Homeland Security asked the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to procure a voting machine, hack it, and report findings back so DHS could pass them to the White House. The request reportedly included a directive not to notify the voting machine manufacturer if flaws were discovered. CISA staffers were said to be alarmed, as the agency's mandate is to defend election infrastructure. The request was never acted on.

Justice Department charges 28 green card holders in California voting sweep

tags: politics, legal, immigration
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Federal prosecutors charged 28 lawful permanent residents in California with illegally registering or voting as part of a statewide operation the Justice Department calls Operation Protect the Vote, with 11 arrested. Charges include false statements on naturalization applications and fraudulent voter registration, and prosecutors allege 21 defendants cast ballots, some in multiple elections. Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter said the conduct causes "real damage to real elections," while California Attorney General Rob Bonta said the administration "has provided us with no facts of any ineligible voters." The department said it has charged 113 people in 20 states over the past seven weeks; the arrests come two weeks before the Nov. 3 midterms and follow a federal lawsuit seeking to block California from counting mail ballots from 20,000 people the government identified as "likely" noncitizens.

Administration expands denaturalization effort weeks before midterms

tags: immigration, politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration has launched what is described as the largest denaturalization effort in American history, targeting naturalized citizens including Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, whose citizenship officials have threatened to revoke. The Department of Homeland Security is carrying out the effort weeks before the November midterm elections. Critics characterize the campaign as voter intimidation intended to discourage naturalized citizens from going to the polls.

Claims that US control of Starshield is affecting Ukraine's front-line defences

tags: war, politics, tech
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Reporting circulating around the Kharkiv strike alleges that Starshield, the military variant of Elon Musk's Starlink used on Ukraine's front lines to detect and counter incoming threats, was interfered with. Musk has said the only person with final authority over how Starshield is used is the President of the United States, and the system operates under a US government contract administered through the Pentagon. The claims are attributed to two anonymous administration sources and a similar report said to have been given to President Zelensky, and have not been independently confirmed.

Alberta votes 76% to remain in Canada

tags: politics, energy
sources: @groundnews

Alberta voters rejected a path toward secession, with unofficial results from Elections Alberta showing 76.4% voting to remain in Canada and 23.6% voting to begin the process toward a binding separation referendum, with more than 1 million ballots counted. Separatists in the oil-producing province argue the federal system gives them too few seats in Parliament and that national climate policy threatens their fossil fuel industry. Premier Danielle Smith announced the vote in May; Prime Minister Mark Carney campaigned against secession in Calgary last week, saying "the frustrations that many Albertans have felt are real." Separatist leaders had travelled to Washington this year seeking backing from the Trump administration.

France weighs local curfews after weekend of riots

tags: politics, policing
sources: @groundnews

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu asked local authorities to impose partial curfews following a weekend of rioting across France, saying the measures must be local and partial and that putting all of Paris under curfew was out of the question. He added the government could declare a state of emergency if needed. The unrest began a month ago with high school protests over school conditions and broadened into demonstrations over the cost of living and public services. More than 500,000 people marched Saturday and the Interior Ministry reported nearly 2,500 arrests, with rioters looting shops and setting fires that destroyed the 19th-century town hall in Limoges and the tourist office in Lyon.

Data center expansion is displacing farmland and straining water supplies

tags: tech, climate, environment
sources: @carolinegleich

About one third of hyperscale data centers are built on former farmland, and Food and Water Watch reports the land required globally is expected to triple over the next five years. Texas lost 2,000 farms in 2025, more than any other state, and has become a data center hotspot, with farmers there reporting dry wells and contamination after construction. Developer money is inflating land prices: Amazon paid $700 million in Virginia for farmland valued at $115 million, and a Kentucky farmer was offered $8 million for land worth a fraction of that. Residents in Kingsborough, North Carolina won a two-year moratorium that halted a $19.2 billion data center.

Georgia officer fired for giving ICE agent husband access to Flock cameras

tags: surveillance, immigration, policing
sources: @aaronparnas

The Savannah Police Department terminated six employees, including an officer who gave her husband, an ICE agent, access to the Flock license plate camera system. The access was used to conduct nearly 1,000 license plate searches. The department's public safety communications manager told Newsweek that unauthorized access to police technology by anyone is a breach of the department and of public trust.

Mississippi attorney general rules police killing of 1-year-old justified

tags: policing, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced that the June police shooting that killed 1-year-old Kohen Wiley in a Walmart parking lot in Senatobia was justified and that no charges will be filed. The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation said the driver drove toward officers responding to a shoplifting call and nearly struck one before an officer fired; the child's mother, Vellesiya Wiley, says they had gone to buy diapers, that the driver was moving away from officers, and that she held her baby up to show police a child was in the car. A preliminary autopsy released by the family's lawyers in July suggested the fatal bullet was fired through the side of the vehicle. No one was charged with shoplifting, and family attorney Ben Crump is demanding release of the officer's body camera footage.

Military spouse detained by ICE at Texas naval base

tags: immigration, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Giovanna Perez was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement on Sept. 21 after arriving at a Navy base in Texas with her four children to collect the family's military ID cards. Perez has lived in the United States since she was six, has no criminal record and no deportation order. Her husband Pedro enlisted in the Army and the family had applied for Parole in Place, a program intended to protect the families of service members; that application appears to have been used to locate her.

Hegseth overhauls military inspector general complaint system

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth is rewriting the rules governing the military's Inspector General system, the channel through which service members report fraud, abuse, dangerous commanders and sexual assault. Under the overhaul, anonymous complaints will generally be rejected, complaints deemed "non-credible" can be unilaterally dismissed, and individuals who file frequently will be flagged. Hegseth described the existing system as "weaponized" but offered no supporting evidence.

Supreme Court rejects bid to restore 9/11 plea deals

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Supreme Court declined to reinstate plea agreements that would have spared accused 9/11 mastermind Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and two co-defendants from execution. The death penalty remains available at their military trial, which is scheduled for 2028.

Supreme Court to review 158-year-old ban on home distilling

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

The Supreme Court agreed to decide whether a federal ban on distilling liquor at home, enacted in 1868 to curb tax evasion, is constitutional. The Hobby Distillers Association and one of its members sued, arguing the ban exceeds Congress' taxing power; a federal district court struck down the law and the 5th Circuit upheld most of that ruling. Solicitor General D. John Sauer called the decision "erroneous," arguing Congress barred home stills because they are harder to inspect and tax, while the distillers' lawyers said "there is no limit to the government's claim of power to criminalize local conduct that might conceal taxable activity." Violators currently face fines, up to five years in prison and possible forfeiture of their homes; arguments are expected next year with a decision due by late June or early July.

Dominion Energy spending on Virginia campaigns amid $67 billion NextEra merger

tags: energy, politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

According to Virginia Mercury, Dominion Energy is spending millions of dollars on political campaigns across Virginia while pursuing a merger with Florida-based utility NextEra. 13 News Now reports the merger is worth $67 billion, and Virginia lawmakers have raised concerns that it could raise costs for residents. NextEra is separately facing pressure in Florida over withheld documents concerning a ghost candidate scheme used in state senate elections.

Vance calls Epstein files protester an illegal immigrant as he is removed

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas

Vice President JD Vance had a protester demanding the release of the Epstein files removed from an event, stating as he did so that the man was an illegal immigrant. No basis for the claim was given. The crowd chanted "USA" as the protester was ejected.

Brazilian right-wing candidate accused of using AI-generated campaign video

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Flavio Bolsonaro, a right-wing candidate in Brazil, is accused of producing AI-generated campaign videos intended to build female support. Side-by-side comparisons show an original clip of a man replaced by a blonde woman in the altered version. The allegations come amid growing use of AI-generated content in Brazilian elections.

Britain pushes back after Hegseth questions allies' role in Afghanistan

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The British government responded after Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth questioned how many NATO allies meaningfully contributed to combat in Afghanistan. Britain cited the 457 British service members who died during the war.

Fort Hood soldiers turning to food banks as survey finds widespread food insecurity

tags: defence, economy
sources: @oafnation_actual

A new investigation found active-duty soldiers at Fort Hood relying on food pantries to feed their families. A military family survey reported food insecurity among 57% of enlisted-family respondents, compared with 13.7% of officer-family respondents. The findings come amid renewed scrutiny of military pay, housing costs and billions in supplemental housing funds.

Afghanistan veteran fatally shot by Connecticut officer during welfare check

tags: policing, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Jakub Dziemaszkiewicz, a 43-year-old Army combat veteran and father of two young sons, was fatally shot by a Connecticut police officer during a welfare check. His former wife said he survived two helicopter crashes and an IED explosion while serving in Afghanistan. Authorities have not explained what led to the shooting, and a state investigation is underway.

Ramaswamy ad features Amy Acton's estranged mother

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee for governor of Ohio, released a campaign advertisement featuring Dr. Amy Acton's birth mother calling her a liar. Acton was sexually abused at age 12 by her mother's husband, who was arrested; her mother lost custody and remained married to the abuser until his death. Acton's brother said in a statement that Ramaswamy had "stooped to such a despicable low as to attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at 12 years old" into a political talking point.

Musk pledges a SpaceX share to every child in America

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Elon Musk said on social media that he will give one SpaceX share to "every kid in America" next year, calling it the first of many. The post came a day after Anthropic announced it would place 5% of its shares into a public benefit fund, with up to 2% more for every 50% rise in company value above a set threshold; responding to that announcement, Musk wrote "I recommend giving the shares directly to the public." With about 72 to 73 million children in the US and SpaceX stock closing at $146.03 on Friday, the pledge would be worth more than $10.5 billion. Musk has not announced eligibility rules, distribution dates or how families would receive the shares.

MAGA influencer removed from Ken Paxton campaign event

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Thelma Louise, a Republican influencer with more than 200,000 followers, said she was asked to leave a Ken Paxton campaign event by his manager while recording footage to share online. She said she does not know why she was singled out. The removal has drawn criticism from Texas Republicans questioning the campaign's handling of a supporter.

Trump and Vance face repeated heckling at public events

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump was heckled six times during an appearance in Kansas, a state he won comfortably. Trump, Vice President JD Vance and other Republican officials have faced similar interruptions at events across the country. Trump has publicly characterised the hecklers as paid protesters.

Trump says New Mexico should change its name

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

During an appearance on his affordability tour, President Trump said New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America because, in his words, "we're not Mexico." The remark came as part of his economic messaging push.
